query: What is discussed in episode 7 between minutes 26 and 28?
answer:
In the first half of that segment the hosts explain that **no machine can decide, in general, whether an arbitrary program will ever halt**—the classic halting problem. They point out that this isn’t just a current limitation; it’s a proven impossibility, so no amount of cleverness or faster hardware can get around it, and because the halting problem is unsolvable, a universal mechanical procedure for deciding every mathematical statement can’t exist either (Episode 7, 26:22‑27:51).

Right after, they shift to the **Church‑Turing thesis**. They note that Alan Turing and Alonzo Church arrived at the same notion of “computable” from two very different angles—Turing’s machines and Church’s lambda calculus—and that both definitions capture exactly the same set of computable functions. From this convergence they argue that the Turing machine model essentially defines what computation is, and that every real‑world computer or programming language can be simulated by a basic Turing machine given enough time and tape (Episode 7, 27:52‑29:21).
